intro: North Macedonia is home to Macedonians, a large Albanian community and several smaller groups.

chapters.title: People and languages
text: Macedonians, who speak a South Slavic language written in Cyrillic, are the majority; Albanians are about a quarter of the population, and Albanian is also an official language. There are Turkish, Roma and Serb minorities. Most Macedonians are Orthodox Christians and most Albanians Muslim.
Skopje is the capital. Mother Teresa was born there in 1910.

chapters.title: Daily life
text: Many young people have emigrated, so the population is shrinking. Family gatherings, coffee and strong home-made rakija are part of daily life.

keyTerms.meaning: Languages including Macedonian, Bulgarian, Serbian and Croatian.
